title: Resolve Tracking Area Code (TAC) to name
description:
Add option to resolve TAC to name and new fields with result of resolution:

`gtpv2.tai_tac` -> `gtpv2.tai_tac_name`

`s1ap.tAC` -> `s1ap.tAC_name`

1. [TACs config file](/uploads/c1a50c1ccc5721f6f39744d76a0eb74e/tacs)
2. [Example GTPv2](/uploads/0a43fd5ec835fc1e7d60c0b61886916b/gtpv2_tac.pcapng)
3. [Example S1AP](/uploads/a923fe134d8bf690fa20aa187f3708dc/s1ap_tac.pcapng)

Maybe consider enhancing pcap-ng name resolution block to include tac as well?
TAC name resolution is very specific and at present moment no such option nor for VLAN, PC (MTP3) and etc, but only for IPv4/IPv6. And I'm not sure this feature is needed somobody.

@kor44 I checked out your feature here. I like it! Though the way we utilize TAC is the high byte is a city, or large area. The the low byte is added to signify a smaller area. You see that in the MME query to find sgw/pgw pairing as well. So HB is generally what we concern with. Not sure if you use the same way, but a "range" would be beneficial. I'm thinking close to the what the subnet file does. Or just a similiar look up, but have it just look at the highbyte.  Have you thought about that use case, or working on something around those lines?

For my case this solution is more than enough. I have DB and export all TAC/name pairs by single SQL command. 

But I understand what you mean: make file with records like as specified in "3GPP TS 23.003 (19.4.2.3)" for "iDNS like lookup": `lb<TAC-low-byte>.hb<TAC-high-byte> <area_name>`

For example:
```
*.hbAB     big_area_1
lb01.hbAB  big_area_1_city_1
lb02.hbAB  big_area_1_city_2

*.hbCF  big_area_2
```

I thought about this but decided it's too complex. In case you will change TAC name resolution, please keep current simple file format.

@@ -975,6 +976,24 @@ unsigned ipv6_oat_hash(const void *key);

 gboolean ipv6_equal(const void *v1, const void *v2);
 
+/**
+ * @brief Resolve an TAC to its area name.
+ *
+ * Returns a string containing the host name associated with the given IPv4
+ * address, or a numeric string in the format `"%d.%d.%d.%d"` if no name is found.
+ * The returned string is managed internally and must not be freed by the caller.
+ * It will be released when address hashtables are cleared (e.g., due to preference
+ * changes or redissection).
+ *
+ * @note This function may increase persistent memory usage even when host name
+ *       resolution is disabled. It may be deprecated in favor of `get_hostname_wmem()`
+ *       for better memory management.
+ *
+ * @param addr IPv4 address in host byte order.
+ * @return     Constant string containing the resolved host name or numeric address.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC const char *tac_name_lookup(const unsigned addr);
+
 #ifdef __cplusplus
 }
